studies.Title: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
studies.Authors: Guo KF, Zhang Z, Wang JY, Gao SL, Liu J, Zhan B, Chen ZP, Kong CZ
studies.Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
studies.Population: Patients with bladder carcinoma and healthy persons
studies.comparison_type: Bladder carcinoma cases versus healthy controls (mean urinary/serum zinc concentrations)

sample_size.excerpt: To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 81 + 130 = 211

cases.excerpt: Since there are few studies of the effect of trace elements in bladder carcinoma in China, the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach. To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.

comparison.excerpt: The results showed urinary Ca, Zn and serum Cu levels of the study group to be significantly higher (P<0.05) than those of he control group.

design.excerpt: the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach

effect_size.excerpt: We observed an inverted U-shaped relationship between toenail zinc concentrations and risk of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: relative to low-level zinc, medium-level zinc had a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.25), but an inverse association that was not significant for high-level zinc (β = − 0.30; 95% CI − 0.41 to 0.01).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We observed an inverted U-shaped relationship between toenail zinc concentrations and risk of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: relative to low-level zinc, medium-level zinc had a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.25), but an inverse association that was not significant for high-level zinc (β = − 0.30; 95% CI − 0.41 to 0.01).
